messages.subject_clean: Error when retrieving a model save as .rds
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I, some time ago, run a model using glmmTMB and saved it as an .rsd object. Then, I could 'load' the model again using the readRDS command. So it worked well.

Now, when the revision time has come, I ran the same code but I am not able to get to the model results. When I type:

m1 <- readRDS('Model_unprotIBA2_log.rds')
summary(m1)

I get:

> summary(m1)
Error in if (REML) { : argument is of length zero

And if I when I ran:

> m1
Formula:
LogAbu ~ Anomaly_std + NEnessSpp_std + Unprotected_IBA + Winter_std +
    Unprotected_IBA * Winter_std + NEnessSpp_std * Unprotected_IBA +
    Winter_std * NEnessSpp_std + Anomaly_std * NEnessSpp_std +
    Winter_std * NEnessSpp_std * Unprotected_IBA + (1 | site) +      (1 | species)
Data: UnprotIBA
     AIC      BIC   logLik df.resid
 6031107  6031274 -3015541  2707636
Error in retape() :
  INTEGER() can only be applied to a 'integer', not a 'NULL'

I would like to sketch the model estimates but I can't get the model back. Do you have an idea why is this happening and how to solve this?

I can provide the rds object (or any other info) if needed.

Thank you very much for your time and help.

Diego

--

messages.body_plain:
Hi Diego,

The latest version expects all models to have a REML argument. Sorry but essentially models fit with the old glmmTMB are not compatible with glmmTMB after this change. I would recommend refitting your model with the new version. If that is extremely inconvenient and you’re sure the old version didn’t have any bugs (see https://github.com/glmmTMB/glmmTMB/blob/master/glmmTMB/inst/NEWS.Rd) then you could install an old version of the package
(https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/glmmTMB/) and use that to summarize your old model.

Since this question is more about glmmTMB than about TMB, it would be more appropriate for the R-sig-mixed list.

Cheers,
Mollie

messages.subject: Spatial glmmTMB does not converge error solutions
messages.subject_clean: Spatial glmmTMB does not converge error solutions
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am new to glmmTMB and experiencing convergence issues using a spatial glmmTMB model, despite a lack of such errors with an aspatial model. I have emulated the recommendations at: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/glmmTMB/vignettes/troubleshooting.html, to no avail. My data are count data at 576 locations and I'm modeling with only one variable; this should not be an issue of overparameterization.

I am attaching a subset of my data. In addition, here is a sample of the code I have used:
library(sp)
library(MASS)
library(car)
library(ape)
library(sjstats)
library(spaMM)
library(spdep)
library(matlib)
library(glmmTMB)

data <- read.csv("data_file.csv", header=TRUE) ##File saved to online repository

#----------Aspatial zero-inflated glmmTMB() model---------------
asp <- glmmTMB(Tot_Lar ~ 1 + NEAR_DIST, data = data, family = nbinom2(link="log"), ziformula= ~1)

#Check model convergence
asp$sdr$pdHess
## return: TRUE

##Morans I: Spatial Autocorrelation
asp$residuals <- as.vector(residuals(asp))
x <- data$Longitude
y <- data$Latitude
distMat <- as.matrix(dist(cbind(x,y)))
invDistMat <- 1/distMat
diag(invDistMat) <- 0
moran <- Moran.I(asp$residuals, weight=invDistMat) ##Null hypothesis is there is no spatial autocorrelation
moran
##Spatial autocorrelation remains because p < 0.05; see ?Moran.I with respect to the null hypothesis

#------------Spatial zero-inflated​ glmmTMB() model-------------------
#Matern Model, following recommendations at https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/glmmTMB/vignettes/covstruct.html
n <- nrow(data)
locs <- numFactor(subset$Longitude,subset$Latitude)
group <- factor(rep(1,n))
mod.mat0 <- glmmTMB(Tot_Lar ~ 1 + scale(NEAR_DIST, center=T, scale=T) + mat(locs + 0 | group), data=data, family=nbinom2(link="log"), ziformula =~1)

##Convergence error; see fixef(), following recommendations at https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/glmmTMB/vignettes/troubleshooting.html
fixef(mod.mat0)

Does anyone have any recommendations as to how to potentially fix the spatial model's convergence errors? Could it be a structural issue of, "mat(locs + 0 | group)," or something else? If someone could also expound on what the syntax "mat(locs + 0 | group)" represents in a glmmTMB() model with a Matern spatial variance-covariance structure that would be particularly helpful as well.

Many thanks in advance.

Cheers,
April

Consider the vector container,

vector<matrix<Type> > V(a);

where each element is equal to,

matrix<Type> m(i,j);

Is it possible to extend V into higher dimensions,
such that V could be indexed as,

V(a, b, c, ..., z)( , ),
where V(a, b, c, ..., z) is of type matrix<Type> with i rows and j cols

Effectively what i'm asking is whether the "vector" container
can be transformed into a "multidimensional array" container,
with the constraint that the objects in the container are either
matrix or vector types.

Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Chris

messages.subject: Re: multidimensional containers
messages.subject_clean: multidimensional containers
messages.body_plain:
Starting from your vector of matrices

vector<matrix<Type> > V(a);

you can construct an array of matrices like this:

array<matrix<Type> > A(V, d);

Here, d is the dimension attribute, e.g.

vector<int> d(3);
d << 2,3,4;

There is no limitation on the array dimension, however the multi dimensional array access A(i,j,k,...) is only implemented up to dimension 7:

https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/structarray.html

messages.subject_clean: Error in asMethod(object) : negative length vectors are not allowed
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am trying to run a glmmTMB model on a fairly large dataset (302400 rows x 4 columns). The code works well when I run it only using the first (or last) 200000 rows of data. However, when I include the whole dataset I get this error:

Error in asMethod(object) : negative length vectors are not allowed
Calls: glmmTMB ... mkReTrms -> lapply -> FUN -> KhatriRao -> as -> asMethod

I think it is an error related to memory requirements, but I have been also using large-RAM computers and the problem is still the same. Does someone have suggestions on how to optimize the code or how to use parallel processing or other solutions with glmmTMB? I would greatly appreciate any help.
Below, a reproducible example and the code I am using to run the model.

Thank you
Fabiola

library("glmmTMB")
library("ff")
y3 <- expand.grid(id=paste("A", seq(1,30,1), sep = ""), time=seq(1,10080,1))
y3$y <- rbinom(nrow(y3),size=1, prob = 0.3)
head(y3)
dim(y3) #302400 rows x 4 columns
y3_ff <- as.ffdf(y3)
rm(list=c("y3"))
mod.TMB <- glmmTMB(y ~ sin(2*pi*time/(24*60)) + cos(2*pi*time/(24*60)) + (1|id) + ar1(as.factor(time) + 0 | id), data=y3_ff, family= binomial(link="probit"), ziformula = ~0)
summary(mod.TMB)
